newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan government, NTT agree on break-up plan - paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan government, NTT agree on break-up plan - paper.

text.p: The Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications and Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) have reached a basic agreement to break up the telecommunications giant into a long-distance operator and two regional companies, a financial newspaper reported on Monday.
The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said that the ministry and NTT were also studying a plan to set up a holding company to control the smaller NTT units after the split-up, planned by the end of March 1999.
In February, a key ministry panel proposed that NTT, which holds 80 percent of Japan's market for domestic telecommunications, be broken up to activate the market.

But the government, which owns 65 percent of NTT, postponed a decision on whether to split it up until next year after some members of the then ruling coalition opposed the break-up, saying it might erode NTT's competitiveness.
NTT itself also opposes being split into three different firms, saying that this would weaken its research and development base amid an increasingly competitive global telecommunications market.

The newspaper said that the idea of creating a holding company to control the smaller NTT units could be seen as a compromise which could halt any decline in the NTT's research and development ability after a break-up.
